capabilities.target: private repositories owned by the user

inputs.source: User's chat prompt: 'Have a look at the open issues in my public repo.'
Issue body in the public repository, authorable by any GitHub user

instructions.evidence_locator: runtime notes: PAT scope across every repository the user owns
instructions.note: Nothing in the configuration or the user's request restricts the agent's effective scope to the single public repository under discussion. The credential backing every tool call has repo scope across all of the user's repositories, public and private, so a session that starts as 'look at issues in my public repo' can technically reach private repository contents with no additional authorization.

controls.name: Per-tool-call client approval prompt
controls.decay_rationale: The approval prompt is enforced by the client outside the model, but arguments are collapsed by default so the approver reviews a summary rather than the raw destination and payload (approval_review_mode: model_summary). A more capable or more persuasive model can shape tool call arguments and issue-derived content so the collapsed summary looks routine, and high call volume per session produces approval fatigue (SAFE-T1403).

controls.name: Fine-grained, per-repository scoped credential
controls.decay_rationale: A credential that structurally cannot read private repositories makes cap.read_private_repo unreachable regardless of model behavior.

controls.name: Raw-action approval review for cross-repo or write actions
controls.decay_rationale: Showing the approver the full destination repository and diff content, rather than a collapsed summary, removes the dependence on the model's willingness to disclose what it is doing.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1): public issue instructs agent to read private repo contents and exfiltrate via public pull request

attack_path.note: Untrusted issue body in the public repo carries injected instructions directing the agent to read private repository files and publish them.
Agent calls get_file_contents against a private repository using the broad-scope PAT, which is not limited to the public repo the user asked about.
Agent opens a pull request on the public repository containing the private repository's content; PR creation is is_egress:true and irreversible once content is publicly visible.

forecast.watch_signal: Approval prompt UI changed to auto-approve or batch-approve repeated tool calls; arguments remain collapsed by default with rising calls-per-session (approval fatigue, SAFE-T1403); model version string in config changes; or the PAT scope is widened to additional organizations.

evidence.observation: A single PAT, passed via GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN, backs every tool call including get_file_contents and create_pull_request; there is no separate, narrower credential for the public-repo-only task the user requested.
The token has repo scope across every repository the user owns, public and private, so the same credential used to browse public issues can also read private repository contents.
Anyone on GitHub can open issues in the public repository, making issue bodies an untrusted (U) input capable of carrying injected instructions to the agent.

The client requires approval per tool call, but arguments are collapsed by default and users approve many calls per session, so the approver is scored as approval_review_mode: model_summary, not raw_action, and is subject to approval fatigue.

The user's own request ('Have a look at the open issues in my public repo') authorizes only reading public issues, not reading private repositories or opening pull requests; any such action originates from attacker-supplied issue content, not the user.

recommendations.action: Use a fine-grained, per-repository scoped PAT (or separate credentials for public vs. private repos) so a session opened to browse a public repo's issues has no technical path to read private repository contents.

Change the approval UI to raw_action review for create_pull_request and other write/egress tools: show the full destination repository and diff/content by default rather than a collapsed summary, especially when a private-repo read occurred earlier in the same session.

Bind pull-request destinations to a pre-approved allowlist distinct from any repository read as confidential in the same session, so a session that has read private data cannot silently target a public repo.
Run an input-injection classifier over issue and comment bodies before they enter agent context, and log/flag any that contain directive language aimed at the agent.

rating.rationale: Inherent risk is critical: an untrusted source (public issue, class U) can reach an S3 sink (create_pull_request on the public repo, is_egress:true, carrying confidential data read moments earlier from a private repo via a broad-scope PAT), matching the U-to-S3 cell of the base matrix with no autonomy modifier needed (not A4, no spawning, no self-config). The only control on the path is the per-tool-call approval prompt (ctl.tool_call_prompt), a structural but partially_dependent control because arguments are collapsed by default (approval_review_mode: model_summary). Per rubric section 5 step 2, a summary-mode approval gate credits -2 tiers but the residual floor is moderate, giving residual = moderate. No control severs the path (the PAT is not scoped per-repo), so step 1 credit does not apply. Under the triggers that defeat a model_summary approval gate (model_upgrade, autonomy_increase, control_removal, longer_task_horizon via approval fatigue), the gate stops constraining the path and the finding reverts to its inherent tier, so forecast = critical. The single control whose decay moves the forecast the most is ctl.tool_call_prompt.

limitations: This assessment reflects declared design and configuration as described in the provided artifacts, not observed runtime behavior; no execution logs or transcripts were reviewed.
No system prompt was provided; instruction-level findings are limited to what the runtime notes and MCP configuration reveal.

The GitHub MCP server image is referenced without a version or digest pin (definitions_pinned: false), so its exact tool schema and behavior at any given time could not be verified from the artifacts alone.
The precise organizational boundary of 'every repository the user owns' (personal vs. organization-owned repos) is not specified in the runtime notes and is treated conservatively as broad scope.

Approval fatigue thresholds (calls per session before an approver stops scrutinizing prompts) are not quantified in the artifacts; the forecast treats this as a qualitative trigger rather than a measured rate.
